title: 925 obstacles between you and everywhere
category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Movement inside the West Bank is not a road network with some checkpoints on it. It is an obstacle regime that OCHA counts, item by item, and the count has been rising for three years.

title: Applying for permission to move inside your own territory
category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The permit is the master mechanism. It is discretionary, time-limited, purpose-bound, secret in its criteria, and can be refused by silence rather than by refusal.

title: The flying checkpoint: an obstacle with no location
category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: A staffed checkpoint can at least be routed around. A flying checkpoint is erected without notice on any road at any hour, which means no route is ever reliable and no journey can be planned.

title: The colour of your number plate decides which roads exist
category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The road regime runs on vehicle registration, not on identity documents. A Palestinian-plated car is barred from roads that an Israeli-plated car uses freely, and the rule has never been written down.

title: Area C: 60% of the West Bank you may cross but not use
category_name: Movement, checkpoints and the permit regime
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The Oslo division was meant to be transitional. Three decades on it is the planning regime, and the largest of the three areas is the one where Palestinian building, farming and infrastructure are effectively prohibited.

title: There is no airport, and the one nearby is closed to you
category_name: Borders, crossings and the airport you are not allowed to use
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Gaza's airport was destroyed in 2002. Ben Gurion is an hour from Ramallah and West Bank Palestinians are barred from using it. The only way out is through Jordan.

title: Allenby: the single gateway, and what happens when it shuts
category_name: Borders, crossings and the airport you are not allowed to use
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: One crossing carries the entire outbound movement of the West Bank. A single point of failure is not a design flaw here; it is the design.

title: Rafah, and the price of a place in the queue
category_name: Borders, crossings and the airport you are not allowed to use
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Gaza's crossing to Egypt has operated intermittently for two decades. When it opens, access to it is rationed - and the rationing has a price list.

title: Being refused entry to the place you are from
category_name: Borders, crossings and the airport you are not allowed to use
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Return is not guaranteed. For a Palestinian abroad, going home is an application, and a refusal at the bridge is not appealable from outside.

title: Israel holds the registry that says you exist
category_name: The population registry, the colour of your ID, and residency
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The Palestinian population registry is controlled by Israel. Births, marriages, divorces, deaths and address changes all require Israeli approval before the Palestinian Authority may issue or amend an ID.

title: Green ID, blue ID, and what each one forbids
category_name: The population registry, the colour of your ID, and residency
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Which document you hold is mostly an accident of where a relative was standing in 1967. It determines which roads, cities, hospitals and countries are available to you for the rest of your life.

title: Jerusalem residency as a privilege that can be withdrawn
category_name: The population registry, the colour of your ID, and residency
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: East Jerusalem Palestinians were made permanent residents, not citizens. Permanent residency is revocable, and the criteria for revoking it were widened after the fact.

title: Registered in Gaza, living in the West Bank: illegal at home
category_name: The population registry, the colour of your ID, and residency
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Since 2000 Israel has refused to let Gaza-registered Palestinians change their ID address to the West Bank. People born and raised in the West Bank are classified as illegal aliens in it.

title: A passport that is a travel document, not a nationality
category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The Palestinian Authority passport is accepted by many states as a travel document while conferring none of the things a nationality confers, because the issuing authority is not a state those countries recognise.

title: Statelessness, inherited
category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Refugee status passes down the generations, and most host states have deliberately not naturalised the people living in them for seventy years. The condition is heritable and the number therefore only grows.

title: The document with no national number
category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Jordan's ex-Gaza Palestinians hold a travel document that looks like a passport, functions as a residence permit, expires every two years, and is refused by several of the countries it would most be used for.

title: Naturalising abroad, and the political test attached
category_name: Status, statelessness and a passport that is not a nationality
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: In some states the route out of statelessness now carries a declaration about the conflict itself, which converts a citizenship application into a test of political opinion.

title: The building permit that is not issued
category_name: Land, home demolition and the building permit nobody gets
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Building legally in Area C requires a permit from the Israeli Civil Administration. The approval rate is close to zero and has been for twenty-five years, which means every Palestinian home built there is unlawful by construction.

title: Demolition, at 4.7 structures a day
category_name: Land, home demolition and the building permit nobody gets
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Demolition for want of a permit is not an occasional event. It runs at a measured daily rate and the rate is rising.

title: Punitive demolition: the family pays for the accused
category_name: Land, home demolition and the building permit nobody gets
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Separately from permit demolitions, homes are demolished as punishment for an attack allegedly committed by a family member - frequently before any trial, and always against people not accused of anything.

title: Settler violence at five incidents a day
category_name: Settler violence and the segregated road regime
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Attacks by settlers on Palestinian people and property reached the highest levels OCHA has recorded since it began counting in 2006, and the UN human rights office finds they occur with the acquiescence or participation of security forces.

title: The olive harvest, and being let onto your own land for one day
category_name: Settler violence and the segregated road regime
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The harvest is both the agricultural year and the cultural one. It now runs under a coordination regime that grants access late, briefly, and to a fraction of the land.

title: Impunity, and what it does to the arithmetic
category_name: Settler violence and the segregated road regime
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Where attacks are rarely prosecuted, the cost-benefit facing both the attacker and the victim changes permanently, and the victim's rational response looks from outside like passivity.

title: Administrative detention: held on material you cannot see
category_name: Detention, military courts and the prison system
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Detention without charge or trial, on secret evidence, for renewable six-month periods with no limit on renewals. There is no allegation to answer because none is made.

title: A court system with a conviction rate above 99%
category_name: Detention, military courts and the prison system
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: West Bank Palestinians are tried by military courts. The conviction rate is such that the trial is not meaningfully a contest, and every strategy is built around plea rather than defence.

title: Women in detention
category_name: Detention, military courts and the prison system
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: Women detainees face the general conditions plus a set of specific ones - strip searches, menstrual management with no supplies, and the certainty that detention itself will follow them socially afterwards.

title: No conjugal visits, and what people did about it
category_name: Detention, military courts and the prison system
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: Israel does not grant conjugal visits to Palestinian security prisoners. The response - smuggling sperm out for IVF - is one of the strangest and best-documented adaptations in this dataset, and the state has moved against the children it produced.

title: The medical permit, and the difference between denial and silence
category_name: Health access, referrals and the medical permit
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Specialist care is largely outside Gaza and outside the West Bank's reach, so treatment requires an exit permit. The permit is rarely refused outright; it is more often simply not answered before the appointment passes.

title: Travelling to treatment alone
category_name: Health access, referrals and the medical permit
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: A patient may be approved while the person who would accompany her is not. For children, the elderly and women travelling to unfamiliar cities, the companion permit is the one that decides whether the journey happens.

title: Which illness you have decides your odds at the window
category_name: Health access, referrals and the medical permit
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Approval rates vary substantially by medical specialty, which means the permit system performs a form of triage that no clinician designed and no patient is told about.

title: Evacuation as the only remaining option
category_name: Health access, referrals and the medical permit
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Where the health system is destroyed rather than merely restricted, treatment means leaving the territory entirely - a process with a small quota, a closed crossing and no return guarantee.

title: Giving birth at a checkpoint
category_name: Women: the body, birth, guardianship and personal status law
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: The most documented single intersection of occupation and gender. Labour does not wait for a gate to open, and the road between a village and a maternity ward has soldiers on it.

title: Two authorities, one journey: the guardian rule on top of the permit
category_name: Women: the body, birth, guardianship and personal status law
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: A Palestinian woman in Gaza needs Israel's permission to leave and, since 2021, may be stopped by a male relative's application to a court. Either alone would be a hurdle; together they are a trap with two keys and she holds neither.

title: Personal status law: two territories, two codes, neither written here
category_name: Women: the body, birth, guardianship and personal status law
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: Family law in the West Bank is Jordanian, in Gaza it is Egyptian, and both predate the Palestinian Authority. A woman's rights in marriage, divorce, custody and inheritance depend on which occupation-era statute her postcode inherited.

title: The killing that gets a reduced sentence
category_name: Women: the body, birth, guardianship and personal status law
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: The provision granting a pardoning excuse for so-called honour killings was annulled in 2011. The articles that reduce the sentence anyway were not, and the courts continue to use them.

title: Managing a period when there is nothing to manage it with
category_name: Women: the body, birth, guardianship and personal status law
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: Under siege and displacement, menstruation becomes a logistics problem with no supplies, no privacy, no water and no disposal - and the coping strategy that emerged is pharmacological.

title: Being pregnant while it is happening
category_name: Women: the body, birth, guardianship and personal status law
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: Pregnancy does not pause for a war. Where the health system has collapsed, the ordinary complications become fatal and the ordinary procedures are performed without anaesthesia.

title: Early marriage, and the reasons that are not tradition
category_name: Women: the body, birth, guardianship and personal status law
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: Marriage ages are set at 18 in the West Bank and 17 in Gaza and can be lowered by a judge with a guardian's approval. Where movement, education and income are all constrained, marriage becomes the available route and the constraint is read afterwards as culture.

title: The family unification freeze
category_name: Family separation, reunification and split households
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Since 2002 Israelis and Jerusalem residents have been barred from obtaining status for a Palestinian spouse from the occupied territory. The measure was temporary in 2002 and is still in force.

title: Living together illegally in your own country
category_name: Family separation, reunification and split households
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Where the registry will not align two spouses' addresses, the family lives together in breach of the rules, in constant exposure to detention and forcible transfer.

title: Visiting someone in prison
category_name: Family separation, reunification and split households
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: Prison visits require a permit, a route through several checkpoints, an entire day, and frequently end in refusal at the last gate. The person doing this is almost always a woman.

title: The family spread across four jurisdictions
category_name: Family separation, reunification and split households
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: An ordinary extended family may hold West Bank, Gaza, Jerusalem, Israeli and diaspora documents. No single event - a wedding, a funeral, an anniversary - can lawfully be attended by all of them.

title: The university as a target
category_name: Education, universities and credentials
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Palestinian universities are raided, their students detained in numbers, and UN experts describe this as systematic policy rather than episodic violence.

title: Winning the scholarship and not being able to take it
category_name: Education, universities and credentials
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Admission is the easy part. The visa, the exit permit, the guardian's consent and the crossing all have to align, and each is separately capable of ending it.

title: A qualification from a place the world is unsure about
category_name: Education, universities and credentials
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Credential recognition assumes a stable issuing authority, an archive that can be written to, and a postal route. Where those are damaged, a real degree becomes unprovable.

title: A work permit tied to one employer
category_name: Work, permits, brokers and wage theft
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The permit is issued in an Israeli employer's name after an army security clearance. It binds the worker to that employer, that area and a curfew, which is the structural cause of everything in WRK-002.

title: The broker who sells you your own permit
category_name: Work, permits, brokers and wage theft
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: A permit bound to one employer and issued in scarce quantities produces a black market. It is large, measured by Israel's own central bank, and the worker pays for it out of the wage the permit lets him earn.

title: Wage theft that cannot be reported
category_name: Work, permits, brokers and wage theft
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Where the intermediary collects the wage, the worker often does not know who the employer legally is - which makes every labour protection unusable.

title: Women's work, and why the participation rate is what it is
category_name: Work, permits, brokers and wage theft
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: Female labour force participation is very low, and the usual explanation is culture. The mechanical explanations - checkpoints, childcare, permit exclusion and safety - come first.

title: PayPal serves the settlement and not the village
category_name: Banking, payments and digital financial exclusion
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The clearest single example of digital exclusion drawn along national lines rather than geographic ones: the same territory, two populations, one of which has payment services.

title: Freelancing with no way to be paid
category_name: Banking, payments and digital financial exclusion
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Remote work is the obvious answer to a closed border. The payment layer is where it fails, and the failure is expensive rather than absolute.

title: Compliance as a permanent surcharge
category_name: Banking, payments and digital financial exclusion
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: For Palestinians abroad, financial life is not blocked so much as taxed - additional checks, delays, refused products and worse rates, indefinitely.

title: An economy with somebody else's currency and customs
category_name: Banking, payments and digital financial exclusion
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The Palestinian economy uses the shekel, and its import duties and VAT are collected by Israel and remitted - or withheld - as a political instrument.

title: Held on 2G by spectrum allocation
category_name: Telecom, spectrum and being held on 2G
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Israel controls frequency allocation under the Oslo framework. Palestinian operators got a sliver of spectrum in 1999 and kept it while their subscriber base multiplied twentyfold.

title: The blackout as an instrument
category_name: Telecom, spectrum and being held on 2G
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Connectivity can be cut, and when it is, it removes the ability to call an ambulance, reach family, verify a rumour or document anything.

title: Being surveilled as the default condition
category_name: Telecom, spectrum and being held on 2G
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Phone, movement, social media and facial recognition data are collected at a density that changes what people are willing to say and where they are willing to go.

title: Water that is not drinkable
category_name: Siege: water, power, fishing limits and the dual-use list
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Gaza's only natural water source has been over-pumped and contaminated to the point where almost none of it is fit to drink, and the fixes require imports that the closure restricts.

title: Electricity by the hour
category_name: Siege: water, power, fishing limits and the dual-use list
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: A chronic deficit means power arrives in blocks and everything - study, refrigeration, medical equipment, water pumping - is scheduled around it.

title: Fishing inside a line drawn offshore
category_name: Siege: water, power, fishing limits and the dual-use list
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The fishing zone agreed at Oslo was 20 nautical miles. The enforced limit has been a fraction of that, which converts a fishing industry into a subsistence one.

title: The list of things you may not import
category_name: Siege: water, power, fishing limits and the dual-use list
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The clearest documented absurdity in the whole file: for three years almost everything was banned unless specifically permitted, and the permitted list was never published.

title: Being blamed for the conditions the siege produced
category_name: Siege: water, power, fishing limits and the dual-use list
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Unemployment, aid dependency and a weak private sector are read abroad as evidence about Palestinians rather than as the measured outputs of a closure policy.

title: Thirty-nine professions you may not enter
category_name: Refugee status abroad: Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, the Gulf
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: In Lebanon, Palestinian refugees are barred from dozens of syndicated professions. The bar is not on ability or qualification; it is on the category the person was born into.

title: Not being allowed to own the home you live in
category_name: Refugee status abroad: Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, the Gulf
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Lebanon's 2001 property law bars Palestinians from owning real estate, using a formula that never names them.

title: A status you inherit and cannot exit
category_name: Refugee status abroad: Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, the Gulf
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Host states have largely declined naturalisation as a matter of policy, and the status passes to children, so the condition compounds rather than resolving.

title: Being refused as a refugee, again
category_name: Refugee status abroad: Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, the Gulf
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: When displacement recurs, the neighbouring states publicly refuse to receive the displaced - which is itself a message received by the people being bombed.

title: A database built to stop you being employed
category_name: Diaspora, speech and the professional cost of the identity
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Doxxing operations publish profiles of students and academics with the explicitly stated purpose of preventing their future employment, and internally track firings as a performance metric.

title: Being the designated explainer
category_name: Diaspora, speech and the professional cost of the identity
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: During any escalation, every colleague and acquaintance treats the nearest Palestinian as a spokesperson, an explanation service or a proxy defendant.

title: The cost of a name on a CV
category_name: Diaspora, speech and the professional cost of the identity
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Before any speech, the name alone does work in a hiring process, a tenancy application and a security clearance.

title: Sending money back, and what it takes
category_name: Diaspora, speech and the professional cost of the identity
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Remittance is the mechanism through which obligation, guilt and power are negotiated in a family split by a border - and the payment rails make it expensive and legally exposed.

title: The watchlist, and whose names are on it
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the watchlist
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Airport screening in the US runs on name-based watchlist matching. The best available analysis of the list's composition indicates it is overwhelmingly Muslim names, which makes 'random' additional screening statistically anything but.

title: Held at the border with a valid visa
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the watchlist
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A visa is permission to travel to a port of entry, not to enter. Recent cases show Palestinians with valid documents held for days, without counsel, with no reason given.

title: Redress that does not redress
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the watchlist
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The official remedy for repeated wrongful screening is a complaint programme whose effectiveness is contested by the people who use it and by government auditors.

title: The exit interview at your own departure
category_name: Airports abroad, screening and the watchlist
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Departing from Ben Gurion - for those few permitted - and from several regional airports involves an interrogation calibrated to origin, conducted in public, with luggage opened in front of the queue.

title: A name with no correct spelling
category_name: Names: transliteration, misspelling and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Arabic names have no single canonical Latin transliteration, so the same person's name is legitimately spelled several ways across her own documents - and every system that compares documents treats that as a discrepancy.

title: The identity is frozen before you reach the airport
category_name: Names: transliteration, misspelling and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Modern air travel locks a vetted identity at booking. A mismatch discovered later cannot be corrected at the gate, by anyone, for technical reasons.

title: Being mistaken for someone
category_name: Names: transliteration, misspelling and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A false positive against a watchlist or a sanctions list is not a brief inconvenience; it attaches to the person and reappears at every subsequent check.

title: The officer who decided, and the one who would not have
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A large share of these hurdles are not policy. They are one person's decision on one day, which another person on another day would have made differently - and which is then permanent.

title: The clerical error that becomes your permanent record
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: A wrong date, a wrong spelling, a wrong status code entered once is copied forward by every subsequent system, and the burden of disproving it is entirely the person's.

title: The letterhead
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The single most concise illustration in this dataset of bureaucracy as an instrument: a document about a dying man was refused because of the words printed at the top of it.

title: Being read as a threat before you speak
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The identity arrives in the room first and carries a prepackaged meaning assembled by decades of coverage. Everything after that is spent correcting an impression nobody admits to having.

title: The marriage and relationship market, with the identity priced in
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: The user's brief names this directly and it is real: the identity changes who will partner with you, on what terms, and how the relationship is read by everyone around it - in both directions, at home and abroad.

title: Learning to say nothing
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: Where speech carries permit, employment, visa and naturalisation consequences, silence is the rational strategy - and practising it for years does specific damage.

title: Threat that does not end, so there is no 'post'
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Trauma frameworks assume the event has finished. Under an ongoing occupation the hypervigilance is an accurate reading of the present, which makes most of the treatment literature inapplicable.

title: Waiting, as a permanent condition
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: Almost every hurdle in this dataset resolves into waiting for a decision by someone who owes no answer and keeps no deadline. Sustained uncertainty is a distinct injury from bad news.

title: What it takes out of the work
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The brief asks specifically for the effects on efficiency and growth. They are real, they are large, and they are attributed to the person rather than the conditions in essentially every setting.

title: Back pain, and the fact that it is measured
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: The brief asks about back pain specifically. It is not a figure of speech: somatic symptom disorder has a published prevalence in Palestinian primary care, back pain is the second commonest presentation, and being female roughly doubles the odds.

title: Chronic pain, with the psychological load measured alongside it
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: A Gaza hospital study puts numbers on the combination the rest of this dataset describes: long-duration pain, near-universal psychological distress, and poverty, in the same patients.

title: Stressful working conditions, and the back that carries them
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: The link between the conditions and the body has been measured in the occupational literature too, in the workforce that holds the health system together.

title: The productivity loss nobody has quantified
category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
applies_to_note: Triggered by Palestinian identity, ID, passport or origin, anywhere
summary: The brief asks about effects on efficiency and growth. The honest position is that the mechanism is well evidenced and the magnitude is not, because the study has not been done.

title: Detaining the doctors and nurses
category_name: Torture, deaths in custody and documented atrocities against civilians
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: Medical workers have been detained in numbers, held without charge for very long periods, and - according to multiple monitoring bodies - tortured. The interrogations reportedly concerned their hospitals and colleagues rather than any alleged offence.

title: Dying in custody
category_name: Torture, deaths in custody and documented atrocities against civilians
applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living under the occupation, any gender
summary: The Special Rapporteur on torture records deaths in custody in numbers, with a stated lack of transparency about causes. The most documented individual case is a surgeon who was never charged with anything.

title: Sexual and gender-based violence in detention, found to be policy
category_name: Torture, deaths in custody and documented atrocities against civilians
applies_to_note: Requires both Palestinian identity and being female
summary: The UN Commission of Inquiry concluded that sexual, reproductive and other gender-based violence against Palestinian detainees was not incidental but an intentional policy forming part of standard operating procedures.

title: Attacking the health system itself
